answer: Each identity must register one harbor-to-island route. The route crosses dune sectors, is key-signed and filed on the island ledger for an auditor to recompute and reject reused paths. Registration locks a 20-credit bond and pays 12 credits per dune sector. The shortest route uses 2 sectors and costs 44 credits. As short routes are taken, later routes lengthen by one sector per hundred prior routes, so the 1,000th costs 152 credits and 1,000 fakes pay about 98,000. An honest agent pays 44 once. A route-rental ring fails: a rented log carries the wrong key, so the auditor burns the bond.
